cards.back: conduct research / conduct a study / conduct an experiment. Example: 'The team conducted extensive research into the effects of urbanisation.'
draw conclusions / draw comparisons / draw attention. Example: 'It is difficult to draw definitive conclusions from such a small sample size.'
reach a consensus / reach an agreement / reach a compromise. Example: 'After lengthy negotiations, the committee reached a consensus on the new policy.'
raise awareness / raise concerns / raise questions. Example: 'The campaign was designed to raise awareness about the dangers of plastic pollution.'
pose a threat / pose a risk / pose a challenge. Example: 'Antibiotic resistance poses a serious threat to global public health.'
address an issue / address a problem / address a concern. Example: 'Governments must address the issue of income inequality before it worsens.'
significant impact / profound impact / detrimental impact. Example: 'Social media has had a significant impact on the way young people communicate.'
profound effect / adverse effect / lasting effect. Example: 'Childhood experiences can have a profound effect on adult behaviour.'
growing concern / growing trend / growing demand. Example: 'Air pollution in major cities is a growing concern among health professionals.'
widely accepted / widely recognised / widely regarded. Example: 'It is widely accepted that education is the key to economic development.'
highly controversial / highly effective / highly unlikely. Example: 'The use of animal testing remains highly controversial among scientists and ethicists.'
increasingly important / increasingly difficult / increasingly common. Example: 'Digital literacy is becoming increasingly important in the modern workplace.'
gain insight / gain experience / gain access. Example: 'Through this study, researchers gained valuable insight into consumer decision-making.'
exert influence / exert pressure / exert control. Example: 'Multinational corporations can exert considerable influence over government policy.'
bear resemblance / bear responsibility / bear the cost. Example: 'The current economic situation bears little resemblance to the crisis of 2008.'
play a vital role / play a crucial role / play a pivotal role. Example: 'Education plays a vital role in reducing poverty in developing nations.'
take into account / take into consideration. Example: 'Policymakers must take into account the long-term environmental consequences of their decisions.'
shed light on / shed new light on. Example: 'Recent archaeological discoveries have shed light on the daily lives of ancient civilisations.'
stark contrast / sharp contrast / marked contrast. Example: 'The wealth of the capital stands in stark contrast to the poverty of rural areas.'
vested interest / have a vested interest in. Example: 'Oil companies have a vested interest in slowing the transition to renewable energy.'
foregone conclusion. Example: 'Given the overwhelming evidence, the outcome of the trial was a foregone conclusion.'
empirical evidence / compelling evidence / anecdotal evidence. Example: 'There is strong empirical evidence linking regular exercise to improved mental health.'
underlying cause / underlying reason / underlying principle. Example: 'Poverty is often the underlying cause of many social problems in urban areas.'
inherent flaw / inherent risk / inherent limitation. Example: 'There is an inherent flaw in any system that relies solely on self-reported data.'
make a distinction / make a contribution / make a case. Example: 'It is important to make a distinction between correlation and causation in research.'
give rise to problems / give rise to debate / give rise to concerns. Example: 'Rapid technological change has given rise to new ethical dilemmas in the workplace.'
come to fruition / come to terms with / come to light. Example: 'After years of planning, the government's infrastructure project finally came to fruition.'
overwhelming majority / overwhelming evidence / overwhelming support. Example: 'The overwhelming majority of scientists agree that human activity is driving climate change.'
pivotal moment / defining moment / watershed moment. Example: 'The invention of the internet was a pivotal moment in the history of communication.'
paradigm shift (a fundamental change in approach). Example: 'The rise of artificial intelligence represents a paradigm shift in how businesses operate.'
tackle a problem / tackle an issue / tackle unemployment. Example: 'The city introduced a congestion charge to tackle traffic jams in the centre.'
meet demand / meet a need / meet a deadline. Example: 'Local farms cannot meet the growing demand for organic food.'
implement a policy / implement measures / implement changes. Example: 'Several countries have implemented policies to reduce single-use plastic.'
take action / take measures / take steps. Example: 'Governments must take urgent action to protect endangered species.'
strike a balance (between X and Y). Example: 'Governments must strike a balance between economic growth and environmental protection.'
bridge the gap (between X and Y). Example: 'Free online courses can help bridge the gap between rich and poor students.'
run the risk of / run a business / run a campaign. Example: 'Students who skip revision run the risk of failing their exams.'
reap the benefits / reap the rewards. Example: 'Countries that invest in early education reap the benefits for decades.'
pay attention to / pay the price for / pay tribute to. Example: 'Future generations will pay the price for today's pollution.'
achieve a goal / achieve success / achieve results. Example: 'Regular practice is the most reliable way to achieve results in language learning.'
pursue a career / pursue a degree / pursue a goal. Example: 'More women are choosing to pursue careers in engineering.'
acquire skills / acquire knowledge / acquire a language. Example: 'Young children often acquire a second language more easily than adults.'
boost the economy / boost productivity / boost morale. Example: 'International tourism can boost the local economy in rural regions.'
alleviate poverty / alleviate pressure / alleviate symptoms. Example: 'Affordable housing schemes can alleviate pressure on low-income families.'
exacerbate the problem / exacerbate inequality / exacerbate tensions. Example: 'Rising rents have exacerbated inequality in many major cities.'
place a burden on / place pressure on / place emphasis on. Example: 'An ageing population places a heavy burden on healthcare systems.'
sharp increase / steady increase / slight increase. Example: 'There was a sharp increase in online sales between 2019 and 2021.'
gradual decline / sharp decline / steady decline. Example: 'The graph shows a gradual decline in coal consumption over the period.'
reach a peak / reach a low / reach a plateau. Example: 'Unemployment reached a peak of twelve percent in 2010 before falling steadily.'
rapid growth / steady growth / sustainable growth. Example: 'The city has experienced rapid growth over the last decade.'
carbon emissions / greenhouse gas emissions / cut emissions. Example: 'Electric buses can significantly cut carbon emissions in cities.'
carbon footprint / carbon tax / carbon neutral. Example: 'Flying less is one of the easiest ways to reduce your carbon footprint.'
renewable energy / renewable sources / renewable resources. Example: 'Renewable energy now provides a growing share of the world's electricity.'
sedentary lifestyle / healthy lifestyle / modern lifestyle. Example: 'A sedentary lifestyle increases the risk of heart disease.'
balanced diet / healthy diet / poor diet. Example: 'A balanced diet is essential for children's physical and mental development.'
mental health / public health / physical health. Example: 'Heavy social media use has been linked to poor mental health among teenagers.'
life expectancy / quality of life. Example: 'Life expectancy has risen steadily thanks to better healthcare and nutrition.'
public transport / public services / public opinion. Example: 'Investment in public transport reduces traffic congestion and air pollution.'
living standards / safety standards / academic standards. Example: 'Living standards in East Asia have risen dramatically since the 1980s.'
skilled workforce / ageing workforce / diverse workforce. Example: 'Japan faces serious economic challenges because of its ageing workforce.'
job opportunities / equal opportunities / career opportunities. Example: 'Remote work creates job opportunities for people living in rural areas.'
higher education / compulsory education / tertiary education. Example: 'Many people argue that higher education should be free for all students.'
commit a crime / reduce crime / violent crime. Example: 'Better street lighting can help reduce crime in residential areas.'
heavy burden / financial burden / tax burden. Example: 'Rising energy prices are a heavy financial burden for many pensioners.'
heated debate / ongoing debate / spark a debate. Example: 'The proposal to ban cars from the city centre sparked a heated debate.'
put forward an argument / put forward a proposal / put forward a theory. Example: 'Supporters put forward a convincing argument for a four-day working week.'
hold a view / hold an opinion / a widely held belief. Example: 'Many people hold the view that university education should be free.'
change attitudes / positive attitudes / attitudes towards something. Example: 'Attitudes towards working from home have changed significantly since 2020.'
far-reaching consequences / unintended consequences / serious consequences. Example: 'Banning cars from city centres could have unintended consequences for local shops.'
inextricably linked (with / to). Example: 'Poverty and poor health are inextricably linked.'
